_comment: The API Products for solution 03 — rate limiting is the quota on the product. POST each to /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/products, then deploy per environment with POST /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/envs/<ENV_ID>/products/<PRODUCT_ID>/deploy. apiIds come from GET /api/orgs/<ORG_ID>/apis. Or just ask the Helix Agent to create them — see ../helix-agent-prompt.md.
_the_model: Developer = Consumer. App = Credential (key/client_id + secret). Product = a bundle of APIs + a quota. An app subscribes via a {productId: rank} map. THE QUOTA IS THE RATE LIMIT, counted PER APP by default.
_quota_is_mandatory: Every product MUST carry a quota object. A product with no quota returns 403 'product missing quota configuration' under the default fail_close — it does NOT mean unlimited. Unlimited is limit: -1.
_counting_scope: quota_key_scope defaults to app: a developer with three apps gets three independent buckets. Set it to developer to pool them. Two keys on the SAME app share one bucket, which is why proving isolation needs two separate apps.
_demo_note: The Free tier here is a deliberately tiny 5/min so a 429 appears in six calls and the demo is snappy. Size your real Free tier for evaluation (e.g. 60/min) and add tiers (Enterprise, an unlimited Internal at limit -1) as more products; they are just more entries in this list.
_window_choice: A per-minute window ABSORBS bursts; a per-second window SHAPES them. Contracts written in requests/day are the worst of both — a day's budget can go in seconds.

products.name: posts-free
products.description: Evaluation access. Deliberately tiny (5/min) so the quota is easy to hit in a demo.

products.name: posts-pro
products.description: Normal production access. Sized well above a healthy integration's peak so a legitimate spike does not page anyone, while a runaway loop still hits a ceiling.
